title.narrative: Transport Network Development Investment Program - Tranche 4

description.narrative: ADB approved a multitranche financing facility (MFF) for the Transport Network Development Investment Program (TNDIP) on 12 October 2011 for an amount not exceeding $787 million, and comprising a maximum contribution of $754 million from ADB's Special Funds resources. To date, three tranches of the MFF are under implementation, and the periodic financing request for Tranche 4 has been received from the government.
Increased movement of goods and services and better connectivity for people and businesses in the project areas.

By 2022: Percent of provincial areas connected to the national highway network by paved roads increased from 21% to 42% (2013 baseline: 21%) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Due to the suspension of AFG operations since the fall of the former government on 14 August 2021, all Works and EA's compliance with reporting requirements remain subject to resumption of ADB operations on Afghanistan.
As of 30 July 2021, achieved work is 76.01% against planned work of 100% with elapsed contract period of 96.93%.
The civil work contract and supervision consultant contract of Baharak to Eshkashim road project signed in Nov 2016 and May 2017, respectively. The civil work contractor mobilized in May 2017.
The pilot Operation and Maintenance contract of Kabul to Sarobi road signed on 6 Dec 2016, mobilized in Feb 2017, and completed in Nov 2017. Data Source: MPW and MOTCA socioeconomic surveys
MPW and MOTCA traffic counts

By 2022: Cross border customs clearance procedures and agreements between Afghanistan and Pakistan, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan effectively implemented (2013 baseline: None) Achievement: N Progress/Status: ACD Procurement: Cargo Scanners package was awarded and contract was signed. Delivery did not proceed due to non-issuance of Commitment Letter. Due to the suspension of AFG operations since the fall of the former government on 14 August 2021, all procurement activities, works, and EA's compliance with reporting requirements remain subject to resumption of ADB operations on Afghanistan. Trackers package contract signing on hold.
The international consultant team and two national consultants conducted Time Release Studies (TRS) at selected border crossing points with Pakistan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, and Tajikistan in Q2-Q3 2019.
Afghanistan Railway Authority (AfRA) is working closely on the structural capacity development. Additional consultants were proposed for engagement. As of 12 April 2021, the following consultants have been issued NTPs and have commenced work: Project Manager, Finance Specialist, Procurement Specialist, and Human Resources Specialist. As of 31 July 2021, the following International Experts are under recruitment: Railway Planning and Operation Specialist, Rolling Stock Specialist, Railway Bridge Design and Construction Engineer, Railway Safety and Signaling Design Specialist, and Economic and Finance Specialist.
